prompt_template:
You are answering a biomedical question using only the numbered passages below.

Write your answer as a list of atomic claims, one per line. Each claim must:
  - state exactly one fact
  - be self-contained (resolve every pronoun and implicit subject)
  - end with citations to the passages supporting it, as [n] or [n][m]
  - cite at most {max_citations} passages

Cite only from the passages. If the passages do not answer the question, say so as a single claim
citing the closest passage.

1. Improvement in visual acuity in amblyopic eyes can occur over time. [2]
2. The mean improvement in distance acuity in amblyopic eyes by 12 months was 3.3 lines logMAR. [2]
3. The mean improvement in near acuity in amblyopic eyes by 12 months was 1.9 lines logMAR. [2]
4. The improvement in acuity in amblyopic eyes generally occurred between 1 and 12 months from baseline. [2]
5. The improvement in acuity in amblyopic eyes remained stable over the period of follow up. [2]

1. Physicians are aware that angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors (ACE-I) are associated with characteristic side effects. [1]
2. The characteristic side effects of ACE-I include cough and angioedema. [1]
3. Referrals for side effects of ACE-I have become more frequent. [1]
4. Physicians are not aware of the degree of knowledge on the safety of ACE-I in different medical categories. [1]
5. A questionnaire on side effects of ACE-I was posted to physicians. [2]
6. The questionnaire contained 13 questions. [2]
7. Three hundred twelve physicians were contacted. [5]
8. One hundred fifty-four physicians returned questionnaires that could be analyzed. [5]
9. The mean age of the physicians who returned questionnaires was 45 years. [5]
10. Cardiologists, allergists, and general practitioners (GPs) from the National Healthcare System were among the physicians contacted. [4]
11. The percentage of correct answers regarding the side effects of ACE-I was low. [5]
12. The percentage of correct answers regarding the side effects of ACE-I was 31.9% for cardiologists, 40% for GPs, and 33% for allergists. [5]
13. GPs provided a significantly higher percentage of correct answers with respect to the remaining categories. [5]
14. The time of onset of cough and the action to take were not well understood by physicians. [5]
15. Angiotensin receptor blockers (sartans) can cross-react with ACE-I. [5]

1. The study aims to evaluate local failure patterns in node negative breast cancer patients treated with post-mastectomy radiotherapy including internal mammary chain only. [1]

2. The study analyzed 92 internal or central-breast node-negative tumors with mastectomy and external irradiation of the internal mammary chain at the dose of 50 Gy, from 1994 to 1998. [2]

3. The local recurrence rate was 5% (five cases). [3]

4. The recurrence sites were the operative scar and chest wall. [3]

5. Age less than or equal to 40 years and tumor size greater than 20mm are associated with increased risk of local failure, but the association is not statistically significant. [3]

6. The study did not provide information on whether chest wall irradiation should be included after mastectomy and negative node breast cancer. [3]

1. A total of 149 patients with suspected parotid gland tumors were examined using echo-planar diffusion-weighted MR imaging (epiDWI). [1]
2. The patients were examined using a 1.5T unit. [2]
3. Image analysis was performed by 2 radiologists independently. [2]
4. The intraclass correlation coefficient was computed for the image analysis. [2]
5. Histologic diagnosis was obtained in every patient. [2]
6. A high correlation was calculated among the observers (0.98). [3]
7. ADC values of pleomorphic adenomas were significantly higher than those of all other entities, except for myoepithelial adenomas (P = .054). [3]
8. ADC values of Warthin tumors were different from those of myoepithelial adenomas, lipomas, and salivary duct carcinomas (P<.001, 0.013, and .037, respectively). [3]
9. Mucoepidermoid carcinomas, acinic cell carcinomas, and basal cell adenocarcinomas were not differentiable from Warthin tumors (P = .094, .396, and .604, respectively). [3]
10. A prediction of different histologic subtypes of primary parotid gland tumors is not possible based on ADC values alone. [3]

1. Patients with gastroparesis treated via gastric electrical stimulation showed more sustained improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms over 36 months than those treated via intensive medical therapy. [7]
2. The improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms in patients treated via gastric electrical stimulation was significantly different from baseline (F = 3.03, P<0.017). [7]
3. Patients treated via gastric electrical stimulation demonstrated further improvement in gastrointestinal symptoms at 12, 24, and 36 month follow-up. [7]
4. Patients treated via intensive medical therapy demonstrated further deterioration in gastrointestinal symptoms at 12, 24, and 36 month follow-up. [7]
5. Patients treated via gastric electrical stimulation had significantly improved healthcare resource usage, measured via the IDIOMS, at 12, 24, and 36 month follow-up. [7]
6. Patients treated via gastric electrical stimulation had significantly reduced hospital days compared to baseline. [7]
7. Patients treated via intensive medical therapy had significantly reduced hospital days compared to baseline. [7]
8. No statistical differences were noted between groups in terms of hospital days. [7]
9. Patients treated via gastric electrical stimulation had significantly decreased costs at 24 and 36 months compared to patients treated via intensive medical therapy. [7]
10. Three of nine patients in the intensive medical therapy group died primarily from i.v. access related problems. [7]
11. None of the patients treated via gastric electrical stimulation died. [7]
12. The study found that gastric electrical stimulation is superior to standard pharmacologic therapy in improving GI symptoms, healthcare resources, and long-term health care benefits. [7]

1. Symptoms are reported by 92% of smokers with airways obstruction. [3]
2. The odds ratio for airways obstruction with smoking (>or = 20 pack-years) is 3.73. [3]
3. Smokers with airways obstruction report respiratory symptoms at a higher rate than nonsmokers. [3]
4. The prevalence of respiratory symptoms is higher in smokers with airways obstruction than in those with restriction or normal spirometry. [3]
5. Symptoms are not a reliable predictor of COPD in smokers, as the positive predictive value is only 47%. [3]
6. The sensitivity of symptoms in predicting COPD is 92% in smokers. [3]
7. The specificity of symptoms in predicting COPD is 19% in smokers. [3]
8. The negative predictive value of symptoms in predicting COPD is 75% in smokers. [3]
9. The US Preventive Services Task Force recommends against spirometry in the absence of symptoms. [1]
10. Up to 50% of COPD cases in the United States remain undiagnosed. [1]

1. The patients in question developed slowly progressive myelopathy. [1]
2. The myelopathy in these patients occurred at the cervical cord levels. [1]
3. The patients had abnormal MRI lesions in the cervical cord levels. [1]
4. The patients were infected with human T-lymphotrophic virus type I (HTLV-I). [1]
5. Clinical and neuroradiologic examinations were performed on the patients. [2]
6. The odds of HTLV-I-infected individuals developing HTLV-I-associated myelopathy (HAM)/tropical spastic paraparesis (TSP) were calculated. [2]
7. Anti-HTLV-I antibodies were positive in the serum of all patients. [3]
8. Anti-HTLV-I antibodies were positive in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of all patients. [3]
9. Inflammatory changes were observed in the biopsied sample from spinal cord lesions of Patient 1. [3]
10. Patient 2 had a demyelinating type of sensorimotor polyneuropathy. [3]
11. Two of the three patients examined showed a high risk of developing HAM/TSP in virologic and immunologic aspects. [3]

1. The incidence of symptomatic venous thrombosis in internal patients during hospitalisation is 0.6% [3].
2. The incidence of symptomatic venous thrombosis in patients with a known malignancy is 2.7% [3].
3. The incidence of symptomatic venous thrombosis in patients without a known malignancy is 0.3% [3].
4. The relative risk for venous thrombosis due to malignancy is 10.0 [3].
5. The relative risk for venous thrombosis due to malignancy has a 95% confidence interval of 5.3-18.9 [3].
6. Thrombosis prophylaxis is generally restricted to patients who are immobilised [1].
7. Most studies on thrombosis prophylaxis focus on postoperative venous thrombosis [1].
8. The primary aim of the investigation was to assess whether more rigorous prophylaxis would be feasible [1].
9. The investigation was conducted in patients hospitalised from 1992 to 1996 [2].
10. The findings of the investigation were related to literature reports [2].
11. The question of whether prophylaxis in all patients makes sense is not addressed by the provided passages.

1. Continuous intravenous infusion of epinephrine was administered to pregnant ewes in the study. [2]
2. The study measured uterine blood flow in the pregnant ewes. [1]
3. The pregnant ewes received an intravenous bolus of epinephrine 15 micrograms. [2]
4. The bolus of epinephrine decreased uterine blood flow to 68 +/- 14% of baseline. [3]
5. Continuous intravenous infusion of epinephrine did not decrease uterine blood flow. [2][3]
6. The study found that infusion of all solutions had no effect on uterine blood flow. [2]
7. The study did not examine the effects of continuous intravenous infusion of low-concentration epinephrine on uterine blood flow in pregnant ewes. [1]

1. The temporomandibular joint was examined in a total of 120 joints. [2][3]
2. The presence of articular sounds and physical signs is often insufficient to detect disk displacement. [3]
3. Imaging by static and dynamic high-resolution ultrasound demonstrates considerably lower sensitivity compared to magnetic resonance. [3]
4. Technical difficulties in ultrasound imaging resulted from limited access due to surrounding bone structures. [3]
5. Magnetic resonance is used as the reference test for calculating sensitivity, specificity, and predictive values. [2]
